events.title: Emperor Antoninus Pius Dies
events.description: Antoninus Pius, who ruled Rome for more than two decades, died in 161. His reign was one of the most peaceful and stable in Roman history. Marcus Aurelius succeeded him.
events.significance: His death ended the era of the Five Good Emperors' most tranquil stretch and brought Marcus Aurelius, the philosopher-emperor, to power.

events.title: Napoleon Captures Jaffa
events.description: During his Syrian campaign, Napoleon Bonaparte's forces stormed the coastal city of Jaffa in Palestine. In the aftermath, French troops killed more than 2,000 Albanian captives.
events.significance: The siege and its brutal aftermath remain among the most controversial episodes of Napoleon's career.

events.title: Webster's 'Seventh of March' Speech
events.description: US Senator Daniel Webster rose in the Senate to speak in support of the Compromise of 1850. He urged national unity and concessions over the slavery dispute to keep the Union together.
events.significance: The speech helped pave the way for the Compromise, which delayed the Civil War by about a decade. It also cost Webster the support of many Northern abolitionists.

events.title: Alexander Graham Bell Patents the Telephone
events.description: The US Patent Office granted Alexander Graham Bell a patent for the telephone. Within days he would transmit the famous words calling his assistant to his side.
events.significance: The invention transformed how people communicate and launched a global telecommunications industry.

events.title: 'Bloody Sunday' in Selma
events.description: About 600 civil rights marchers set out from Selma, Alabama, toward the state capital, Montgomery. They were forcefully broken up by law enforcement at the Edmund Pettus Bridge.
events.significance: Televised images of the violence shocked the nation and helped build support for the Voting Rights Act of 1965.
